summary: The Ohio Information Technology Centers (OITC) urges the FCC to retain Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) as an eligible Category Two service under the E-Rate program, emphasizing its cost-effectiveness and importance for schools of all sizes and geographic locations. The OITC argues for improved oversight and application review to address concerns regarding waste, fraud, and abuse rather than eliminating or reducing MIBS funding. The claim that MIBS is essential for ensuring secure, reliable broadband access for schools and libraries is supported by evidence showing its cost-effectiveness and benefits in maintaining network management solutions. The Broadband Coalition on Digital Opportunity emphasizes the importance of Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) for schools and libraries, arguing that limiting or sunsetting the E-Rate program would have significant negative impacts on network reliability, security, and cost-efficiency. The comments from school districts and other stakeholders highlight concerns about the eligibility and implementation of Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) under the E-Rate program. They argue that restricting MIBS eligibility based on district size or location would bear little relationship to the actual operational technical need
